rationale.conceptual: The method is a custom, multi-part finite element formulation (axisymmetric piezoelectric elements, damping, heat diffusion, thermal stress) with several interacting components and non-trivial physics. It requires genuine understanding of piezoelectricity, structural damping, heat transfer boundary conditions, and iterative coupling. This goes well beyond textbook examples.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves mesh generation, initial electromechanical solve, iterative thermal-mechanical loops (heat source calculation, steady-state heat diffusion, mesh update, material matrix update, re-solve), and final extraction of quantities. It is a multi-stage process with dependencies but no exotic tooling; all can be done with standard numerical libraries.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper presents a multi-physics finite element simulation coupling electromechanical vibration, heat generation from mechanical and dielectric losses, steady-state heat diffusion with convection/radiation, thermal expansion, and material property updates. Implementing this from scratch requires non-trivial mathematical translation and careful assembly of several interacting components. The pipeline has multiple stages and an iterative convergence loop, though the mesh scale is modest.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The finite element model of the bolt-clamped transducer is small (tens to a few hundred elements); solving sparse linear systems and iterating a few times requires modest CPU and memory, well under 1 GB, and no external datasets beyond provided material constants.
